newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's unemployment flat at 9.7 pct in Jan.
newsitem.headline: Canada's unemployment flat at 9.7 pct in Jan.

text.p: Statistics Canada said on Friday the unemployment rate remained unchanged at 9.7 percent in January from December.
Note - Labor force, employment and unemployment in millions, on seasonally adjusted basis.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast the unemployment rate to drop to 9.6 percent.
Full time employment rose by 32,400 from the month before, while part time employment fell by 27,300.
Statistics Canada said total employment rose by 91,000 or 0.7 percent since September 1996. Of all the jobs created since September, 80,000 were full-time.
Employment in the goods producing sector was little changed in January and employment in the construction sector rose by 19,000.
The utilities industry lost 11,000 jobs in the month. Employment in manufacturing was little changed after declining by 42,000 in the previous three months.
There was also little change in service sector employment in January, leaving gains in the past year at only 38,000 jobs, Statistics Canada said.
Public employment was virtually unchanged in the month and a strong gain in self-employment was offset by a large decline in private sector employment.
